claims.text: The initial FeCoNi-based alloy is FCC.
An almost equiatomic FeCoNi composition has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Part of the ferromagnetic Co can be replaced by antiferromagnetic Cr to form a near-equiatomic FeCoNiCr alloy.
Near-equiatomic FeCoNiCr retains configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Cr substitution introduces localized antiferromagnetic interactions into the FeCoNi-based alloy.
Replacing Co with Cr can promote nanoscale phase heterogeneity, including ordered and disordered regions.
Composition and annealing conditions can determine the length scale of Cr-associated phase decomposition.
Cr substitution reduces overall ferromagnetic exchange strength.
The Cr-induced magnetic and structural inhomogeneities act as magnetic pinning sites.
These pinning sites impede domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion increases the coercive field.
Near-equiatomic FeCoNiCr will have greater coercivity than baseline FeCoNi or the prior Pd- and Pt-containing FeCoNi derivatives.
Cr substitution may moderately decrease saturation magnetization.
Prior FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives exhibit soft ferromagnetism with low coercive fields.
A controlled fine-scale two-phase structure can aid magnetic pinning.
Excessive Cr substitution may cause an overly large reduction in saturation magnetization.
Excessive Cr substitution may promote unfavorable phase separation.

contradictions.description: Starting from equiatomic FeCoNi, replacing only a fraction of Co with an equivalent amount of Cr cannot by itself produce equiatomic FeCoNiCr; Fe and Ni would remain near 33.3 at.%, while Co and Cr would each be below that level. Producing a near-equiatomic quaternary alloy requires rebalancing all four elements.

The stated baseline emphasizes Pd- or Pt-containing FeCoNi derivatives, whereas the proposed experiment uses ternary equiatomic FeCoNi as its sole control. Thus, the experiment does not directly test the claimed superiority over the declared prior-derivative baseline.
